text: I’ll model the gears as straight-tooth bevel solids generated by lofting involute transverse tooth profiles toward the common pitch-cone apex. The pitch-cone angles follow the 20:30 tooth ratio and 90° shaft angle; backlash will be applied as a 0.3 mm reduction in circular tooth thickness at the outer pitch circles. Because face width and shaft/bore diameter were not specified, I’ll initially assume a 15 mm face width and 18 mm shaft bores, center the common cone apex in the cavity, and use Cartesian cut-cell meshing after verifying the coarse CAD/STLs.

I’m now building the two coarse lofted gear solids from explicit involute profiles. I’ll sample the wheel’s rotational phase and choose a non-intersecting meshing position rather than assuming the tooth indexing is correct.

The coarse phase scan found the expected mesh position at half a wheel pitch (6°); the residual overlap is only 2.6 mm³ and comes from using planar involute sections on intersecting bevel axes. I’ll form the physical solid union before subtracting it from the cavity, so no internal overlap enters the oil mesh, then inspect the resulting fluid volume and boundary faces.

The preview confirms the intended orthogonal bevel arrangement, taper direction, wall exits, and ample cavity clearance. Next I’m classifying the already-booleaned fluid boundary by its generating surfaces: six planar enclosure faces, each cylindrical shaft/bore surface, and the remaining exposed faces of each gear.

The boundary inspection exposed a placement error before meshing: `Cylinder` defaults to centered axial alignment, so both shafts stopped inside the cavity instead of reaching the walls. I’m correcting them to `Align.MIN` with explicit global-axis placement, then recomputing the fluid.

All 862 fluid-boundary faces classify without ambiguity: 6 enclosure faces, 342 pinion faces, 512 wheel faces, and one cylindrical face for each shaft bore. I’m exporting exactly these five face groups as the requested patch STLs, using 0.1 mm tessellation tolerance.

The complete five-STL union is closed even though each individual patch is necessarily open. I’m stopping CAD refinement here and writing the smallest viable cut-cell setup: a 3,315-cell background grid, cavity at level 0, shafts at level 1, and gears at level 2.
`blockMesh` caught a compact dictionary formatting error before creating any cells. I’m expanding the boundary syntax and rerunning only the background grid.
The 3,315-cell background mesh now exists. I’m running the coarse surface-cut and snap pass immediately; quality refinement can follow only if this first mesh fails.
The mesher requires standard empty-case numerics dictionaries even though no solver will be run. I’m adding only those mandatory files and repeating the same coarse meshing pass.
Surface ingestion is successful; OpenFOAM 2512 additionally requires an explicit empty feature list. I’m adding it and continuing.
The compact form parsed `features()` incorrectly despite displaying it. I’m rewriting the controls in conventional multiline OpenFOAM syntax to remove parser ambiguity.
The first actual cut-cell mesh completed with 10,640 cells and all five named surface patches. I’m running `checkMesh` now before spending any effort on visualization or refinement.

The exhaustive geometry diagnostics flag concave cut cells, although all solver-critical bounds pass (max non-orthogonality 45.8°, skewness 2.37, positive volumes, one connected region). I’ll now look at the coarse mesh itself, including a clipped interior view, before deciding whether the standard binding check requires changes.
The VTK conversion succeeded; only the plotting library rejected a three-digit hex color. I’m correcting that display-only issue and rendering the clipped mesh.
The coarse mesh visibly conforms to the cavity and bore opening. I’ll now run the standard binding `checkMesh` (the exhaustive concavity diagnostic is stricter than the normal acceptance check).

The binding check passes: one region, positive volumes, max non-orthogonality 45.83°, max skewness 2.37. I’m making one final patch-colored view and printing the requested geometric measurements directly from the construction parameters.

The coarse mesh is complete and the standard `checkMesh` result is **Mesh OK**. I am declaring it complete without advisory waivers: the five exported patch STLs collectively represent the closed oil boundary, and the meshing point is inside the connected oil region. Assumptions are 15 mm bevel-gear face width and 18 mm shaft/bore diameter because neither was specified.

The advisory checker found a real export defect: tessellating each B-rep face group independently introduced patch-edge cracks and overlapping triangles, even though the same fluid exported as one surface is closed. I’ll fix this by tessellating the complete fluid boundary once, then partitioning that single shared triangle set into the five patch files. This preserves identical vertices and winding across every patch seam.
The corrected patch files now partition all 108,004 triangles of one manifold master surface exactly once. I’m regenerating the mesh from these corrected STLs and rerunning the binding check.
The regenerated mesh again passes `checkMesh` with the corrected manifold patch exports. I’m rerunning the completion gates now.
